Subject: RFP: Dedicated reservation questions (GPU mix / tail latency / cutover)

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is a short questionnaire our procurement and infra teams asked us to complete with vendor responses. High level: CloudNova is planning a phased migration of our chat augmentation service (currently hosted on single-tenant infra) to a vendor-provided reserved pool. Target steady-state throughput ~600 QPS (text generation requests) with 99th pct latency target ~150ms. We expect a 3x peak burst factor during promotions.

We have three asks we want vendor guidance on:
- Recommended GPU mix for mixed-latency workloads (A100 vs H100 vs L4 equivalents) and expected inline 95/99 latency per GPU.
- Reservation sizing strategy (how many reserved slots vs autoscale/burst) and expected provisioning lead times.
- Cutover/migration plan to minimize traffic loss and a fallback strategy if reserved pool reaches capacity.

Deliverables: a short capacity worksheet and a suggested commitment band (monthly v. annual) + any assumptions.

Attached: cloudnova_rfp_questions.pdf (your questionnaire). Can you confirm a timeline to return this by next week?

Irene / team — initial draft answers below (sending as inline bullets so we can iterate):

1) Recommended GPU mix (by workload lane)\- Latency-sensitive generation (99th pct target <=150ms): H100 (sized for lower tail due to larger tensor cores and better mem-bandwidth). Recommend using H100 s for the hot lane.
  - Throughput per H100 (conservative estimate, mixed-length prompts): ~35-45 requests/sec for typical 2-4k token context using Redwood-optimized kernels.
  - Expected 95/99 latencies: ~60–90ms (95th), 110–160ms (99th) depending on prompt length distribution and batchability.
\- Cost-sensitive background generation / offline reranking: A100S / A100 (or quantized H100 variants)
  - Throughput per A100S: ~20-30 reqs/sec (same assumptions), 95/99 latencies ~120–210ms.

2) Reservation sizing & burst policy\- Suggested starting reservation: 8 H100s + 12 A100S equivalents. That maps to an estimated steady-state effective capacity of ~520–700 QPS depending on prompt mix and caching hit rates.
\- Burst strategy: allow burst to dedicated shared pool with autoscaling up to additional 2x for 30-minute windows (subject to availability). Recommend a burst cap of 3x steady-state for 15–60 mins with priority lanes enforced (hot lane first).\- Lead times: reserved capacity provisioning for H100 families: 3–5 business days for dedicated pools in our hosted regions (provisioning time assumes capacity available; private/on-prem timelines differ).

\3) Cutover & fallback plan\- Cutover: phased DNS-weighted cutover with canary traffic (5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%) over 48–72 hours, with traffic steering to lower-cost lane during observed tail spikes.
\- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to a compatible quantized model on the A100S fleet and regional failover to a secondary region (if configured).
\4) Assumptions / recommended commitment bands\- Assumptions: average prompt length 3k tokens, caching expected to reduce per-request compute by up to 18% for repeated prefixes, on-call windows aligned to their business hours.
\- Commitment recommendation: start with a 12-month reserved baseline (8 H100 + 12 A100S) with a quarterly review and a 15% overage buffer (pre-agreed burst credits) for promotional spikes. Annual pricing yields ~17% discount vs monthly commit.
\Attachments: redwood_commitment_workbook.xlsx (workbook with capacity math + cost scenarios).
\Next steps: Vivek — can you validate per-GPU throughput numbers and add any kernel-fit notes? I can draft the commercial blurb and send to Sam.

Thanks,

Ben / Irene — validated the numbers and added kernel-fit caveats inline (keeps formatting simple here):
\- H100 fit: best for transformer-decoder large models where 4k+ context is common. Expect higher memory pressure; we recommend enabling KV-cache compression and our preferred fused attention kernels.\- A100S fit: good cost/perf for quantized variants and shorter average contexts (<2.5k). If CloudNova expects lots of short prompts (chat-style), consider moving extra capacity to A100S and rely on prefix caching.
\Throughput sensitivity:
- If average request grows from 3k -> 5k tokens, per-H100 throughput drops ~30% and tail latency widens; reservation should include a headroom factor of 1.35.
\Slot-level packing & isolation:
- We recommend slot isolation for hot-lane H100s to avoid noisy-neighbor tail spikes; pack A100S aggressively in mixed tenancy.
\I'll append a short cutover checklist for the customer deck; Ben please include the workbook and I'll sign off.
\Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni

Hi Sam / Maria — thanks for the questionnaire. Please find our consolidated responses and the capacity workbook attached. Summary below:

Executive summary:
- Recommended baseline reservation: 8x H100 + 12x A100S (Redwood-hosted Dedicated pool). This yields an estimated steady-state capacity in the 520–700 QPS band depending on prompt mix and prefix-caching efficiency.
- Tail budget: plan for a 15% committed buffer and a 3x short-duration burst allowance (15–60m windows) handled by autoscale + burst credits.
- Cutover plan: phased DNS-weighted ramp (5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%) across 48–72 hours with canary health checks and immediate rollback to prior endpoint if error rate >1.5% or 99th latency exceeds target by >40%.
- Lead times: H100 family provisioning in Redwood-hosted regions typically 3–5 business days. Private/VPC timelines differ and will be handled separately if chosen.

Attachments included:
- redwood_commitment_workbook.xlsx (capacity math, scenarios by prompt-length: 2k / 3k / 5k tokens)
- cloudnova_capacity_plan_notes.pdf (cutover checklist + monitoring playbook)

Commercial notes & next steps:
- Commitment bands: monthly vs 12-mo: we recommend a 12-month baseline for predictability; see workbook for pricing scenarios.
- If you want dedicated isolation for all hot instances we can provide an SLA addendum (requires legal review).
